jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Gabon has no AI-specific law and no published AI strategy; one is being prepared with UNDP. Its binding AI rules are in other texts: the 2023 revision of the data protection law requires an opinion or declaration to the data protection authority (APDPVP) for AI systems that process personal data and adds rights over automated decisions and profiling; the 2023 cybersecurity law bans AI interception of communications without consent; a 2025 digitalisation ordinance names AI-enabled 'Smart-Government'; and a February 2026 ordinance bans harmful deepfakes and requires platforms to detect and label AI-generated content, overseen by the High Authority for Communication.
lead_institutions: Authority for the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from the full texts in the Official Journal. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI guidance from the data protection authority, the digital ministry's numerique portal and the cybersecurity agency. The national AI strategy is still in preparation and is tracked as a lead.

instruments.official_title: Loi n°001/2011 du 25 septembre 2011 relative à la protection des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 001/2011 of 25 September 2011 on the protection of personal data
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament (National Assembly and Senate); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: In force as amended by Law 025/2023 of 12 July 2023 (which repeals contrary provisions of this law). Published in Official Journal No. 74 of 24 October 2011; the gazette header dates the law 24/09/2011 while the signature line reads 'Fait à Libreville, le 25 septembre 2011' (signature date used here).
instruments.summary: Gabon's framework personal data protection law, applying to automated and non-automated processing of personal data and setting up the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data (CNPDCP) with declaration and authorisation regimes. It bars court decisions and other decisions with legal effects from being based solely on automated processing intended to profile a person or evaluate aspects of their personality. It was substantially revised by Law 025/2023, which replaced the CNPDCP with the APDPVP.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Baseline data protection law; contains Gabon's original rule against decisions based solely on automated profiling.

instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament (National Assembly and Senate); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: In force; published in Official Journal No. 218 bis of 15 July 2023. The gazette header dates the law 09/07/2023 while the signature line reads 'Fait à Libreville, le 12 juillet 2023' (signature date used; Ordinance 0011/PR/2026 also cites it as of 12 July 2023). Not yet verified from the official text: publication of the implementing 'norms' for AI systems.
instruments.summary: Comprehensive revision of Gabon's data protection law that replaces the CNPDCP with the Authority for the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy (APDPVP), adds AI and machine-learning definitions, a right to object to decisions based solely on automated processing including profiling, and information duties on the logic of automated decision-making. A section on technological innovation (arts. 177-178) aims to make AI 'trustworthy, human-centred, ethical, sustainable and inclusive', applies to AI technologies designed or used in Gabon, and requires any AI system that includes personal data to be subject to an APDPVP opinion or declaration under a standard; it also bans profiling of children save exceptions authorised by the APDPVP and subjects facial recognition processing to opinion or declaration.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Gabon's main binding text with explicit AI provisions (AI systems processing personal data, automated decisions, profiling, facial recognition).

instruments.english_title: Law No. 027/2023 of 12 July 2023 regulating cybersecurity and the fight against cybercrime in the Gabonese Republic
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament (National Assembly and Senate); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: In force; published in Official Journal No. 218 bis of 15 July 2023. The gazette header dates the law 11/07/2023 while the signature line reads 'Fait à Libreville, le 12 juillet 2023' (signature date used).
instruments.summary: Gabon's cybersecurity and cybercrime law, setting security obligations for operators of networks, information systems and critical infrastructure and defining cybercrime offences. Its only explicit AI provision (art. 38) prohibits any natural or legal person, IT equipment or artificial intelligence from listening to, intercepting, storing or otherwise surveilling communications and traffic data without the users' consent unless legally authorised.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General cyber law with one explicit AI provision (ban on AI-based interception of communications without consent).

instruments.official_title: Ordonnance n°0006/PR/2025 du 12 août 2025 portant réglementation de la Digitalisation en République Gabonaise
instruments.english_title: Ordinance No. 0006/PR/2025 of 12 August 2025 regulating digitalisation in the Gabonese Republic
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic, Head of State, Head of Government (ordinance under art. 99 of the Constitution)
instruments.current_status: Signed 12 August 2025 and published in Official Journal No. 81 of 30 August 2025 (gazette header dates it 11/08/2025; signature date used). A bill to ratify it was presented to the Transitional National Assembly's committee (Assembly website). Not yet verified from the official text: the ratification law.
instruments.summary: Framework ordinance on the digitalisation of state services and public and private bodies, covering dematerialisation of administrative procedures, data collection and sharing, online platforms and payments, guided by principles of universality, interoperability, security, digital inclusion and national private-sector participation. It defines a 'Smart-Government' stage as using artificial intelligence and emerging technologies to make the administration proactive, alongside e-, mobile-, open- and digital-government stages. It sets no AI-specific obligations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Legal basis for digital government that names AI use in the administration ('Smart-Government') as a stage of public-sector digitalisation.

instruments.official_title: Ordonnance n°0011/PR/2026 du 26 février 2026 portant réglementation de l'usage des réseaux sociaux via les plateformes numériques en République Gabonaise
instruments.english_title: Ordinance No. 0011/PR/2026 of 26 February 2026 regulating the use of social networks via digital platforms in the Gabonese Republic
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic, Head of State, Head of Government (ordinance under Law 042/2025 enabling legislation by ordinance during parliamentary recess)
instruments.current_status: Signed 26 February 2026 and published in Official Journal No. 110 of 8 April 2026. As an ordinance it requires ratification by Parliament. Not yet verified from the official text: ratification, implementing regulations (art. 54) and the technical standards for AI-content detection.
instruments.summary: Regulates users, publishers and hosts of social networks and digital platforms whose content is accessible in Gabon, with a chapter on AI-generated content (arts. 32-34) that bans sexual deepfakes of identifiable people without consent, harmful deepfakes attributing false statements, sexual depictions of minors and AI imitation of state institutions for disinformation, gives depicted persons a 24-hour takedown right and lets the High Authority for Communication or prosecutors order independent audits of platforms' AI detection and labelling systems. Platforms must within 12 months deploy automatic detection of AI-generated content, apply a visible permanent label to it and hand origin metadata to the HAC; identity-usurpation offences committed through AI carry up to 10 years' imprisonment and a fine of up to 50 million FCFA.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Gabon's first binding rules specifically on AI-generated content, deepfakes and AI-content labelling.

coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. apdpvp.ga 403; cnpdcp.ga, numerique.gouv.ga, anincc.ga proxy 502. Journal search in French. Ordinances 0006/PR/2025 and 0011/PR/2026 recorded binding_regulation per brief rule for orders; ratification laws not found. Gazette header dates differ from signature dates for Laws 001/2011, 025/2023, 027/2023 and Ord. 0006/PR/2025; signature dates used. Convention 108 act not found. Units covered: Law: Official Journal portal (journal-officiel.ga) searched in French: AI provisions found in Law 025/2023 (data protection), Law 027/2023 (cybersecurity) and Ordinance 0011/PR/2026 (social networks, deepfakes, AI-content labelling); Law 001/2011 read. Penal Code (Law 042/2018) checked: no AI provision. Ordinance 0006/PR/2025 on digitalisation (AI 'Smart-Government' definition) found. No AI-specific law or pending AI bill found; National Assembly site search for 'intelligence artificielle' returned only the hearing on the digitalisation ordinance ratification bill.; Government: Ministry of Digital Economy, Digitalisation and Innovation website searched: only an AI hackathon event page, no AI strategy, guideline or public-sector AI document. Ministry and Directorate-General organisation decrees (0388/PR/MENNTI 2024, 0440/PR/MENNTI 2024, 0268/PR 2025, 0489/PR/MENDI 2025, 00030/PR 2026, 00050/PR/MENDI 2026) checked: no AI provisions. National AI strategy in preparation (lead).; Ministries: Searched, nothing found: no AI documents from education, health, justice, defence, finance, labour or interior ministries in the Official Journal or official sites.; Regulators: APDPVP/CNPDCP deliberations in the Official Journal: no AI guidance or AI decision found (APDPVP and CNPDCP websites not reachable). ARCEP website searched: only a news item on ARCEP's AI regulatory priorities presented in London, no AI guidance document. High Authority for Communication: AI-content powers come from Ordinance 0011/PR/2026; no HAC AI guidance found. No AI material from the central bank (BEAC/COBAC are regional), cyber agency (ANINCC site unreachable) or standards body.. Not reached: apdpvp.ga (HTTP 403); cnpdcp.ga (unreachable); numerique.gouv.ga (unreachable); anincc.ga national cybersecurity agency (unreachable). Could not verify: APDPVP website (403) and CNPDCP, numerique.gouv.ga and ANINCC sites (unreachable): any AI guidance published only there could not be checked.; Convention 108: no Gabonese ratification/accession act found in the Official Journal; Gabon does not appear among Convention 108 parties in Council of Europe material seen, so set to null.. strategy, government-governance, ethics, risk-assurance, procurement, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
